name: Anmeldung (Registering your address)
description: Register your address with the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) after moving into a new home in Berlin. Required by German law within 14 days of moving in.
eligibility: Anyone moving into a new home in Berlin — new residents and people relocating within Berlin — must register within 14 days of moving in.
requiredDocuments: Valid ID card or passport
Completed 'Anmeldung einer Wohnung' registration form
Wohnungsgeberbestätigung — a written confirmation from your landlord or property owner that you moved in, legally required since 2015
processingTime: Done on the spot at your appointment; you receive a registration confirmation (Meldebescheinigung) immediately.

name: Personalausweis beantragen (Applying for a German ID card)
description: Apply for a German national identity card (Personalausweis), the standard proof-of-identity document for German citizens aged 16 and up.
eligibility: German citizens aged 16 and older with a registered address in Berlin (a secondary residence is accepted for a valid reason, with an extra fee). Children under 16 may apply with parental/guardian consent. Non-Berlin residents, tourists, and Germans living abroad can apply through the State Office for Citizen and Order Affairs.
requiredDocuments: Current digital biometric passport photo
Previous ID document, if available (even if expired)
Valid passport, if you have one
Birth certificate or marriage/civil partnership certificate, if you have never had an ID or your name differs from the civil registry
For newly naturalized citizens: your previous nationality's passport/ID and your naturalization certificate
For minors: written parental/guardian consent, plus a copy of the non-present parent's ID
fees: €27.60 for applicants under 24; €46.00 for applicants 24 and older. A secondary-residence surcharge (€13.00), in-office photo (€6.00), and direct mail delivery (€15.00) can apply on top of that.
processingTime: Around 3 to 4 weeks under normal circumstances; individual cases can take longer. An emergency provisional ID can be requested if needed sooner.

name: Reisepass beantragen (Applying for a German passport)
description: Apply for a German passport (Reisepass), the travel document required for international trips outside the EU/Schengen area.
eligibility: German citizens registered in Berlin. Personal appearance is mandatory for all applicants, including minors; for applicants under 18, a legal guardian must submit the application together with the child. Unregistered persons, tourists, and Germans living abroad can apply through separate channels.
requiredDocuments: Current digital biometric passport photo
Previous passport or ID document, if available
Valid identity document (e.g. personal ID card)
Birth, marriage, or partnership certificate, if you've never held these documents before or your personal data differs from the registry
For minors: parental consent form and a copy of the absent parent's ID, if only one parent attends
For naturalized citizens: previous passport/ID or identification certificate, plus the naturalization certificate
fees: €37.50 for applicants under 24; €70.00 for applicants 24 and older (doubled if Berlin is not your primary residence). Express processing costs an extra €32.00, a 48-page passport an extra €22.00, an in-office photo €6.00, and direct mail delivery €15.00.
processingTime: Up to 8 weeks under the standard process; express service can take as little as 4 business days if the application is submitted before 11 a.m.

name: Führungszeugnis beantragen (Requesting a certificate of good conduct)
description: Request a certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis) — an official extract from the Federal Central Register showing whether you have a criminal record, often required by employers or authorities.
eligibility: Anyone registered (or habitually resident) in Berlin who is at least 14 years old. EU citizenship is only required for the separate 'European certificate of good conduct'.
requiredDocuments: Completed application form (available online, in person, or by post)
For written/postal requests: signed application plus a copy of your ID (passport or national ID card)
For a certificate sent directly to an official body: that recipient agency's name, address, file reference, and the certificate's purpose
For an extended certificate: written authorization from the requesting organization
Proof of bank transfer for the fee, if applying by mail
fees: €13.00. Fee waivers exist in specific circumstances — check the official page for details.
processingTime: About 2 weeks for a standard certificate; about 4 weeks for a European certificate.

name: Erstzulassung eines Fahrzeugs (First registration of a vehicle)
description: Register a brand-new, never-before-registered vehicle for road use in Berlin and receive its registration certificates and license plates.
eligibility: Individuals with their primary residence registered in Berlin, or businesses/associations with their registered seat or a branch in Berlin, registering a factory-new vehicle that has never been registered before. A secondary residence in Berlin is not sufficient.
requiredDocuments: Completed application form for vehicle first registration
Valid ID card or passport
Vehicle Registration Certificate Part II (Fahrzeugbrief) or an equivalent operating permit
EC Certificate of Conformity (COC)
Valid motor insurance confirmation with an eVB number
SEPA direct debit authorization for vehicle tax
For businesses: commercial register extract, business registration, and IDs of managers
For associations: association register extract and IDs of the leadership
For minors: parental consent
fees: From €22.22 for an online application, or at least €30.60 for an in-person application; license plate production is billed separately.
processingTime: Not stated exactly on the page; registration documents are sent by post a few days after registration.

name: Kraftfahrzeug ummelden — nach einem Umzug nach Berlin (Re-registering a vehicle after moving to Berlin)
description: Re-register a vehicle you already own after moving your primary residence to Berlin, updating its registration certificate to your new Berlin address.
eligibility: Vehicle owners/keepers who have moved their primary residence to Berlin and whose vehicle is already registered in Germany. A secondary residence in Berlin is not sufficient. Businesses/associations qualify if they have a seat or branch in Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Application for re-registration without change of keeper
Valid ID card or passport
Current Vehicle Registration Certificate Part I
Vehicle Registration Certificate Part II, only if requesting a new Berlin license plate
Current emissions/safety inspection report (HU-Prüfbericht)
SEPA direct debit mandate, unless you're keeping your current plate
Old license plates, if applicable
For businesses: business registration and commercial register extract
fees: €17.50 basic fee, plus additional charges depending on the specifics (e.g. a new license plate).
processingTime: Not stated exactly on the page; the office notes new appointment slots are released daily depending on capacity.

name: Fahrerlaubnis — Ersterteilung beantragen (Applying for a first driving license)
description: Apply for a first driving license (Fahrerlaubnis) in Berlin, covering vehicle classes from mopeds to trucks and buses.
eligibility: Applicants with their principal residence in Berlin (exceptions possible with approval from the home-residence authority) who meet the minimum age for the license class they're applying for; personal appearance is required. Applications can be submitted up to 6 months before reaching the minimum age.
requiredDocuments: ID card or passport
One current biometric passport photo on paper (none printed on-site)
Name and address of your driving school and chosen testing center
First aid training certificate (exemptions for medical professionals and healthcare workers)
Vision test certificate, no older than 2 years (classes AM, A1, A2, A, B, BE, L, T)
Medical vision examination, no older than 2 years (classes C, C1, CE, C1E, D, D1, DE, D1E)
Certificate of physical and mental fitness, no older than 1 year (classes C, C1, CE, C1E, D, D1, DE, D1E)
Functional and performance test, no older than 1 year (classes D, D1, DE, D1E)
Certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis), for classes D, D1, DE, D1E — must be requested separately at a citizen office
Proof of professional qualification, if applying for the FQN alongside classes C or D
fees: €45.90 standard, or €45.10 for classes AM or L only; €6.32 extra for delivery by registered mail. The FQN certificate costs €35.00 including domestic delivery.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check directly with the licensing authority.

bookingInfo.office: Bürgeramt (any district citizens' office) or the Berlin-wide driving license booking system

name: Umschreibung einer ausländischen Fahrerlaubnis aus einem EU-/EWR-Staat (Converting an EU/EEA driving license)
description: Convert a driving license issued by another EU or EEA (EWR) country into a German driving license.
eligibility: Holders of a valid (or recently expired) driving license issued by an EU or EWR member state, with their main residence in Berlin. If Berlin is only a secondary residence, a justified exception must be approved by the main-residence authority. Personal appearance is required.
requiredDocuments: ID card or passport
One current biometric passport photo on paper (bring your own — none printed on-site)
Your original EU/EWR driving license (valid or expired)
If the license was lost or stolen: detailed particulars, any available copies, or confirmation from the issuing country

For truck/bus classes (C/D): medical fitness certificate, vision examination, a functional performance test (class D only), a certificate of good conduct (class D), and proof of professional qualification where applicable
processingTime: Not stated on the page; check current processing status (Bearbeitungsstände) with the licensing authority.

bookingInfo.office: Bürgeramt (any district citizens' office) or Landesamt für Bürger- und Ordnungsangelegenheiten (LABO), Puttkamerstr. 16-18

name: Umschreibung einer ausländischen Fahrerlaubnis aus einem Nicht-EU/EWR-Land (Converting a non-EU/EEA driving license)
description: Convert a driving license issued by a country outside the EU/EEA (a 'third country') into a German driving license.
eligibility: Holders of a valid, original national (not international) driving license issued by a country outside the EU/EWR, with their main residence in Berlin. Personal appearance is required, and non-EU/EWR citizens must also present a residence permit.
requiredDocuments: ID card or passport
Residence permit, if you are not an EU/EWR citizen
One current biometric passport photo on paper
Name and address of your driving school and chosen testing center
Your original national (not international) foreign driving license, still valid
Certified translation, if the license isn't in German or English
First aid training certificate (third-country license holders only)
Vision test, for car/motorcycle classes A and B
Medical/psychological examination, for certain truck/bus license classes
fees: €37.50 for a conversion without an exam, or €45.10 if an exam is required.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check with the licensing authority for current processing times.

bookingInfo.office: Bürgeramt (any district citizens' office) or Landesamt für Bürger- und Ordnungsangelegenheiten (LABO), Puttkamerstr. 16-18

name: Gewerbe anmelden (Registering a business)
description: Register a new self-employed commercial business (Gewerbe) with a fixed place of operation in Berlin.
eligibility: Natural persons operating as sole traders, partners in a partnership (OHG, GbR, KG), or legal entities (GmbH, AG, UG) starting a commercial business with a fixed place of operation in Berlin. Does not cover free professions (Freiberufler), agriculture, or other activities exempted under §6 GewO.
requiredDocuments: Completed business registration form (online or as a PDF)
Valid government-issued photo ID or passport
Residence permit, if you are not an EU citizen
Current commercial register extract, for already-established companies
Articles of association and shareholder consent, for newly forming legal entities
Representative authorization form, if a legal entity has multiple authorized representatives
fees: €26.00 per sole proprietor or per partner in a partnership; €31.00 for a legal entity with one authorized representative (plus €13.00 per additional representative); €15.00 for online submission.

bookingInfo.office: Ordnungsamt (district order office responsible for the business location)

name: Eheschließung anmelden (Registering to get married)
description: Register your intent to marry at a Berlin registry office (Standesamt) so you can hold the wedding ceremony within the following 6 months. Covers couples where both partners are German citizens born in Germany, without foreign-nationality involvement.
eligibility: Couples where both partners are German citizens by birth, born in Germany, with no foreign-nationality involvement in the marriage.
requiredDocuments: Valid, signed passport or ID card for both partners
Extended registration certificate (erweiterte Meldebescheinigung) showing marital status, no older than 14 days, if your main residence is outside Berlin
Certified extract from the birth register with annotations (not a birth certificate), no older than 6 months

If previously married or in a civil partnership: certified marriage/partnership register extract showing dissolution, or the certificate plus the final divorce/dissolution decree (or death certificate if widowed)
Birth certificates of any children you share
Paternity acknowledgment and custody declarations, if applicable
Certified German translations of any foreign-language documents, plus apostille/legalization where required
fees: €45.00 for registration and examination of the marriage prerequisites; €40.00 extra to marry at a different registry office; €80.00 outside business hours; €75.00–€150.00 outside official premises. A German marriage certificate costs €12.00 (additional simultaneous copies €6.00 each).
processingTime: Not stated on the page. Registration is valid for 6 months, during which the marriage must take place.

bookingInfo.office: Standesamt (district registry office where either partner resides)

name: Geburt eines Kindes melden (Registering the birth of a child)
description: Register the birth of a child born in Berlin with the registry office (Standesamt) responsible for the birth district, so a birth certificate can be issued.
eligibility: Applies to any birth that takes place in Berlin, regardless of where the parents live; the responsible registry office is determined by the district where the birth occurred.
requiredDocuments: Birth notification from the hospital/birthing center, or a birth certificate for home births
Valid ID (passport or national ID card) for both parents
Mother's birth certificate
Father's birth certificate, if applicable
Marriage certificate, if the parents are married
Paternity acknowledgment and custody declaration, if the parents are not married
Divorce or death documentation, if the mother was previously married
Signed name declaration form from both parents
Certified translation and apostille/legalization for any foreign documents
fees: Registering the birth itself is free. A birth certificate, certified registry extract, or international birth certificate each cost €12.00 (additional copies issued at the same time cost €6.00 each).
processingTime: Not stated on the page. For home births, registration must happen within one week.

bookingInfo.office: Standesamt (district registry office in the district where the birth occurred)

name: Einbürgerung — Verleihung der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit beantragen (Applying for German citizenship)
description: Apply for German citizenship by naturalization (Einbürgerung) after meeting Berlin residency, language, and other legal requirements.
eligibility: Foreign residents of Berlin with uninterrupted lawful residence in Germany for at least 5 years (3 years if married to a German citizen), holding an appropriate residence permit, who commit to the German constitution, are not dependent on Bürgergeld/Sozialhilfe (with some employment-related exceptions), have no significant criminal record, have German language skills at B1 level, can show knowledge of the German constitutional and social order (e.g. via the 'Leben in Deutschland' test), and have health and long-term care insurance.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport or ID card
Vital records: marriage/divorce certificates, adoption decrees, if applicable
Employment or income documentation
Language certificate proving at least B1-level German
Test certificate for 'Leben in Deutschland' or another accepted citizenship test
Registration confirmation (Meldebestätigung)
Proof of health and long-term care insurance
Rental contract or proof of property ownership
Parental consent form, for children under 16 with shared custody
fees: €255.00 per adult applicant; €51.00 for a child under 16 applying together with a parent. Additional costs may apply if release from a previous nationality is required.
processingTime: The office noted around 40,000 pending cases as of January 2024, leading to extended processing times.
